question: Could the universe have been expanding forever into the past, with no beginning at all?
answer: Not under broad conditions, says a 2003 theorem. Borde, Guth and Vilenkin showed that any universe that has, on average, been expanding must have a boundary in its past. But the proof uses classical physics, and a quantum theory of gravity might escape it. It rules out one kind of endless past, not every kind.
move: A proof is only as strong as the conditions written into it.
ask: Which rule I live by holds only under conditions I have stopped checking?
source: Borde, Guth & Vilenkin, Physical Review Letters, 2003
